what: The Challenge of Cell Clustering Evaluation
title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: single-cell RNA-seq analysis, clustering algorithms aim group cells similar transcriptomic profiles. However, several challenges arise: Parameter Sensitivity: Clustering results highly sensitive resolution parameters -clustering: High resolution may split biologically homogeneous populations -clustering: Low resolution may merge distinct cell types Lack Ground Truth: True cell type labels rarely available scClustEval addresses challenges quantitative, data-driven approach.

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: self-projection method treats cluster evaluation classification problem: “clustering biologically meaningful, classifier able accurately distinguish cells different clusters based gene expression profiles.”

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: Given expression matrix 𝐗∈ℝn×p\mathbf{X} \\mathbb{R}^{n \times p} nn cells pp features, cluster labels 𝐲∈{1,...,K}n\mathbf{y} \\{1, ..., K\}^n: 𝐗=𝐗train∪𝐗test \mathbf{X} = \mathbf{X}_{train} \cup \mathbf{X}_{test} Stratified sampling ensures cluster kk contributes proportionally: nktrainntrain≈nktestntest≈nkn \frac{n_k^{train}}{n^{train}} \approx \frac{n_k^{test}}{n^{test}} \approx \frac{n_k}{n}

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: train multi-class classifier f:ℝp→{1,...,K}f: \mathbb{R}^p \rightarrow \{1, ..., K\} predicts cluster membership. default L1-regularized logistic regression: min𝛃−∑=1ntrainlog⁡P(yi|𝐱i,𝛃)+λ||𝛃||1 \min_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} -\sum_{=1}^{n_{train}} \log P(y_i | \mathbf{x}_i, \boldsymbol{\beta}) + \lambda ||\boldsymbol{\beta}||_1

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: confusion matrix 𝐂∈ℝK×K\mathbf{C} \\mathbb{R}^{K \times K} computed test set: Cij=|{x:ytrue(x)=∧ypred(x)=j}| C_{ij} = |\{x : y_{true}(x) = \land y_{pred}(x) = j\}| : - CiiC_{ii} (diagonal): correctly classified cells cluster ii - CijC_{ij} (-diagonal): cells cluster ii misclassified cluster jj

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: R1 normalization measures pairwise confusion rate relative correct classifications: R1(,j)=max⁡(CijCjj,CjiCii) R1(, j) = \max\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{jj}}, \frac{C_{ji}}{C_{ii}}\right) Interpretation: - R1=0R1 = 0: Perfect discrimination - R1>1R1 > 1: misclassifications correct classifications (severe confusion) - High R1 indicates clusters potentially merged
code: library(scClustEval)  # Example confusion matrix cmat <- matrix(c(   90, 5, 3,    # Cluster A: 90 correct, 5 misclassified as B, 3 as C   8, 85, 7,   # Cluster B: 8 misclassified as A, 85 correct, 7 as C     2, 12, 86   # Cluster C: 2 as A, 12 as B, 86 correct ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE) rownames(cmat) <- colnames(cmat) <- c("A", "B", "C")  # Compute R1 normalization r1_mat <- normalize_confmat_r1(cmat) print(round(r1_mat, 3))

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: R2 normalization measures overall confusion proportion dataset: R2(,j)=Cij+CjiNtotal R2(, j) = \frac{C_{ij} + C_{ji}}{N_{total}} Ntotal=∑,jCijN_{total} = \sum_{,j} C_{ij}. Interpretation: - R2 represents fraction total cells confused clusters ii jj - Values range 0 1 - Useful identifying globally important confusions
code: # Compute R2 normalization r2_mat <- normalize_confmat_r2(cmat) print(round(r2_mat, 4))

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
code: library(ggplot2) library(gridExtra)  # Create data for visualization df_r1 <- as.data.frame(as.table(r1_mat)) colnames(df_r1) <- c("True", "Predicted", "R1")  df_r2 <- as.data.frame(as.table(r2_mat)) colnames(df_r2) <- c("True", "Predicted", "R2")  p1 <- ggplot(df_r1, aes(x = Predicted, y = True, fill = R1)) +   geom_tile(color = "white") +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", R1)), color = "white", size = 5) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = "gray90", high = "#d62728") +   labs(title = "R1 Normalization", subtitle = "Pairwise confusion rate") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))  p2 <- ggplot(df_r2, aes(x = Predicted, y = True, fill = R2)) +   geom_tile(color = "white") +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", R2)), color = "white", size = 5) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = "gray90", high = "#1f77b4") +   labs(title = "R2 Normalization", subtitle = "Global confusion proportion") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))  grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: Clusters exceeding confusion thresholds connected adjacency graph: Aij={1if R1(,j)>θR1 R2(,j)>θR20otherwise A_{ij} = \begin{cases}  1 & \text{} R1(,j) > \theta_{R1} \text{ } R2(,j) > \theta_{R2} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: Louvain algorithm identifies communities (groups confused clusters) maximizing modularity: Q=12m∑ij[Aij−kikj2m]δ(ci,cj) Q = \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{ij}\left[A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m}\right]\delta(c_i, c_j) : - mm = total number edges - kik_i = degree node ii - cic_i = community assignment node ii - δ\delta = Kronecker delta

title: Algorithm Principles and Mathematical Foundation
text: Cutoffs progressively relaxed outer iteration: θR1(t+1)=θR1(t)−ΔR1 \theta_{R1}^{(t+1)} = \theta_{R1}^{(t)} - \Delta_{R1} θR2(t+1)=θR2(t)−ΔR2 \theta_{R2}^{(t+1)} = \theta_{R2}^{(t)} - \Delta_{R2}

text: Logistic Regression (multinomial L1): P(y=k|x)=exp⁡(βkTx)∑j=1Kexp⁡(βjTx) P(y=k|x) = \frac{\exp(\beta_k^T x)}{\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp(\beta_j^T x)} Random Forest prediction: ŷ=mode{h1(x),h2(x),...,hB(x)} \hat{y} = \text{mode}\{h_1(x), h_2(x), ..., h_B(x)\} hbh_b individual decision trees.

title: Introduction to scClustEval
text: scClustEval (Single Cell Clustering Evaluation) R package evaluating optimizing single-cell RNA-seq clustering results using self-projection machine learning approaches. package implements iterative optimization strategy : Trains classifier distinguish clusters Evaluates prediction accuracy via cross-validation Identifies cluster pairs difficult discriminate Merges confused clusters iteratively target accuracy reached

text: Let’s create synthetic dataset known cluster structure demonstrate assessment workflow.
code: # Generate synthetic single-cell data set.seed(42) n_cells <- 600 n_features <- 50 n_clusters <- 4  # Create expression matrix with distinct clusters X <- matrix(nrow = n_cells, ncol = n_features) labels <- character(n_cells) cells_per_cluster <- n_cells / n_clusters  for (i in 1:n_clusters) {   start_idx <- (i - 1) * cells_per_cluster + 1   end_idx <- i * cells_per_cluster      # Each cluster has a distinct mean expression profile   cluster_mean <- rnorm(n_features, mean = i * 2, sd = 0.5)   X[start_idx:end_idx, ] <- matrix(     rep(cluster_mean, cells_per_cluster) + rnorm(cells_per_cluster * n_features, sd = 1),     nrow = cells_per_cluster,     byrow = TRUE   )   labels[start_idx:end_idx] <- paste0("Cluster_", i) }  colnames(X) <- paste0("Gene_", 1:n_features)  cat("Data dimensions:", nrow(X), "cells x", ncol(X), "features\n") cat("Clusters:", unique(labels), "\n")
